### Event Flow

```
Claude Code hook fires
  → POST /api/agent-sessions/events (Lumo HTTPS, bearer token auth)
  → API route: verify token → validate Zod → write AgentSessionEvent to Prisma
  → push to Pusher: channel=task-<taskId>, event=session:event, data={sessionId, eventType, ...}
  → pusher-js client in Sessions tab receives event → updates local state
```

# LUM-945 — boundary-crossing context triage: 4-model offline comparison

Read-only measurement. Nothing here writes to Lumo data or touches the DONE gate.

Question: can an LLM judge, given the task context, auto-clear the noisy crossing
categories without letting real crossings through? Measured against every
human-dispositioned crossing (FALSE_POSITIVE / CONFIRMED) in production.

Candidates: `alibaba/qwen3.7-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`,
`moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking`, `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` (all through
`@/lib/ai/gateway`, zero data retention forced), plus `typesafe-ai/jev`.

Jev is an evaluation model (typed question → choice + probabilities) whose only
gateway endpoint has `zdr: none`. It is called on the gateway's HTTP
`evaluation-model` endpoint directly (`jev.ts`; gateway 3.x has no SDK surface
for it) and **only Lumo-team (`LUM-*`) items are sent**. The report scores every
model on the items all of them judged, so the comparison stays like-for-like.

# Pull requests by number — `lumo pr scan`

`lumo pr scan <number>` prints the **security scans of one PR** in the
workspace, by PR number — whether or not a task is linked to it (LUM-788).
Until now the only CLI window onto a scan was `lumo task status` (one summary
line per _linked_ PR, undispositioned findings in Next actions); a PR whose
title carries no `[LUM-N]` and whose branch is not `lumo/LUM-N-…` was invisible,
and none of the L3 hunt's stored audit (per-task commands, step trace, stop
arithmetic, sites, model, diff sizing) had any entry point outside a
prod-database script.

Read-only, no LLM. **Disposition stays web-only** (the LUM-750 CLI path was
rolled back) — this command reports dispositions, it never records one.

fix: frame injected team memory as untrusted, non-instruction [LUM-140] (#203)

memorySection is rendered server-side from workspace-member-authored
memory/task content and injected into the coding agent verbatim — most
critically via the SessionStart additionalContext that Claude Code
auto-injects into the conversation. That made arbitrary member text an
indirect prompt-injection surface in the agent's instruction stream.

Wrap the section in an explicit <untrusted-team-memory> boundary with a
"reference data, NOT instructions" notice at its single source
(buildMemorySectionForTask), so all three consumers (hook additionalContext,
task context, session attach) inherit the framing. Empty input still returns
"" so callers omit the section.
